input:
The left-hand derivative of f(x) = [x] sin(πx), at x = k, k is an integer and [.] is the greatest integer function, is

Options:
A. (-1)ᵏ(k - 1)π
B. (-1)ᵏ⁻¹(k - 1)π
C. (-1)ᵏkπ
D. (-1)ᵏ⁻¹kπ

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Find the left-hand derivative (LHD) of f(x) = [x] sin(πx) at an integer point x = k.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: The definition of LHD at x = k is lim(h→0⁺) [f(k-h) - f(k)] / (-h). For small h > 0, k-1 < k-h < k, so [k-h] = k-1. Also f(k) = [k] sin(kπ) = 0.

key_concepts: Left-Hand Derivative (LHD) definition: LHD = lim(h→0⁺) [f(k-h) - f(k)] / (-h)
Greatest integer function property: For 0 < h < 1 and k ∈ ℤ, [k-h] = k-1
Trigonometric reduction: sin(π(k-h)) = sin(kπ - πh) = (-1)ᵏ⁻¹ sin(πh)

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Apply the definition of LHD at x = k, evaluate [k-h] as k-1 and f(k) as 0, simplify sin(π(k-h)), and use the standard limit sin(πh)/h → π.
logical_steps: Step 1: Write LHD formula: lim(h→0⁺) [f(k-h) - f(k)] / (-h)
Step 5: Compute limit as h → 0 and match option

step_3_trig_simplification.sin_expansion: sin(kπ - πh) = sin(kπ)cos(πh) - cos(kπ)sin(πh) = 0 - (-1)ᵏ sin(πh) = (-1)ᵏ⁺¹ sin(πh)

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Using definition: LHD = (k-1) · d/dx[sin(πx)]|_{x=k} = (k-1) · π cos(kπ) = (k-1) π (-1)ᵏ = (-1)ᵏ(k-1)π. Perfectly matches option A ✓
